references.text: God promised to rain bread from heaven to test the people, which is the background for the manna in the wilderness
The Israelites called the bread manna, which they ate in the wilderness
The Israelites ate manna for forty years until they reached the inhabited land
The people complained that they had only manna to look at in the wilderness
The people spoke against God and called the manna wretched food
The manna ceased on the day after they ate from the produce of the land
God gave them manna from heaven and water from the rock
God let manna rain down upon them and gave them grain from heaven to eat
God satisfied the people with bread from heaven when they prayed
God humbled and tested the people with manna to teach them that man lives by every word from God's mouth
Discipline does not seem joyful at the moment, but later yields the peaceful fruit of righteousness - a parallel to God's testing to bring about good in the end
Jesus refers to the manna the fathers ate in the wilderness and calls himself the true bread from heaven
Jesus mentions that the fathers ate manna in the wilderness and died
Paul notes that all ate the same spiritual food, which refers to the manna
